(θ, s) is the interior's surface coordinate (blueprint frame.ts); reading both fields of a point is how every user of it starts, not a copied procedure. It crossed the idiom threshold only because more files made the names rarer.
The skin shader mirrors core's hash32 in TSL on purpose, so the GPU picks the very panels gen/skin.ts does (checked bit for bit with a compute pass).
Each mover advances itself by one time step: the player's body, the flyer inside, the flyer outside. Different physics, the usual name.
The flyer inside (up toward the axis, above the ground) and the one outside (clearance to every body, float64 over 50,000 km) share a name, not their rules.
Speed of the flyer inside grows with height above the ground; outside, with the clearance to the nearest body. Same idea, different geometry.
Each camera turns by pointer movement in its own frame (walker: heading on the curved floor; flyer outside: yaw around the ecliptic pole).
